name: Muttekopf
kurzbeschreibung: The Muttekopf (2,774 m) in the Lechtal Alps lures alpinists with the Imst Via Ferrata, the historic Muttekopfhütte, and views stretching to the Zugspitze.
beschreibung:
Overview

The majestic and prominent Muttekopf reigns supreme at 2,774 meters above sea level as the commanding summit overlooking the town of Imst in the Tyrolean Oberland. Nestled in the eastern Lechtal Alps, this mountain composed of fractured Hauptdolomit and solid Wetterstein limestone is a beloved playground for seasoned mountaineers, rock climbers, and ambitious hikers. Across its eastern flanks lies the scenic Muttekopfkar basin, where the historic Muttekopfhütte at 1,934 meters provides shelter and hospitality. The summit cross opens up an expansive panorama spanning the Inn Valley, the Gurgltal, the glaciated Ötztal and Stubai Alps, and north to the Wetterstein massif with Germany's Zugspitze. Historically, the peak achieved fame through early alpine exploration by the Austrian Alpine Club in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

Route & Requirements

Thanks to the Imster Bergbahnen chairlifts, the long valley ascent can be shortened considerably: two sections of comfortable chairlifts whisk hikers from Hoch-Imst via the Untermarkter Alm up to Alpjoch at 2,050 meters. From the upper station, the well-marked Drischlsteig – a panoramic path blasted directly into the rock and secured with steel cables – descends in about thirty minutes to the Muttekopfhütte. From the hut, hikers climb through wide scree basins and over a secured rocky ridge to the summit cross (approx. 2.5 hours from hut, difficulty T3, surefootedness essential). Experienced climbers can take on the celebrated Imster Klettersteig, one of Tyrol's oldest and sportiest via ferratas (graded C/D, safety kit required). Sturdy boots with Vibram soles and weatherproof gear are essential.

Visit & Arrival

The Imst chairlifts run daily from mid-May to late October. Free car parking is provided at the valley station in Hoch-Imst. By public transport, take the train to Imst-Pitztal station and board city bus line 1 or 2 up to Hoch-Imst. The Muttekopfhütte is fully staffed from mid-June to early October, offering comfortable dorm beds and traditional Tyrolean cuisine.

Tips

Pair your mountain descent with an adrenaline rush on the Alpine Coaster Imst, the world's longest alpine coaster spanning 3.5 kilometers down to the valley. On the sunny hut terrace, sample homemade Kaiserschmarrn with lingonberry jam after your climb.
preis: Mountain trails freely accessible; Imst chairlift rides fee applies (Sections I and II)
oeffnungszeiten: Mountain hut and trails open from mid-June to early October
